additionalLifecycleRepairs.issue: A browser could disconnect before a delayed terminal/open was admitted under the still-live gateway-worker channel.
additionalLifecycleRepairs.change: Coordinated with the runtime reviewer: GatewayServer registers a fresh UUID worker owner via /connect before completing every browser WebSocket handshake; worker-bound RPC requires that live owner. The worker validates active owner/channel membership at admission, after reading the body and immediately before native write. Disconnect revokes the owner; channel loss clears all of that channel's owners. Internal channel IDs and owner IDs are stripped before browser events; routed terminal events use owned:true.
additionalLifecycleRepairs.scope: This report owns GatewayServer, WorkerClient, terminal browser consumer and corresponding gateway/web tests. Runtime endpoint/lease registry changes and tests are recorded by the runtime reviewer.

additionalLifecycleRepairs.issue: An unknown /connect response could otherwise leave a late active registration after best-effort cleanup.
additionalLifecycleRepairs.change: WorkerClient captures the exact event channel for connect/disconnect, fences that channel on failed confirmation, never replays registration, and ignores cleanup for a retired channel. Request headers carry the captured event-channel ID; queued HTTP writes recheck the same live channel immediately before beforeWrite.
additionalLifecycleRepairs.verification: worker-client tests simulate lost registration confirmation, verify channel termination, then confirm old-owner cleanup cannot close the replacement channel. A delayed HTTP socket connect after channel replacement is rejected before ledger beforeWrite.

additionalLifecycleRepairs.issue: A rejected duplicate browser handshake could release another handshake's pending-slot guard.
additionalLifecycleRepairs.change: Final reread found and fixed #connecting reservation ownership: only a request that acquired the slot may delete it in finally.
additionalLifecycleRepairs.verification: HTTP fixture pauses owner registration and submits two duplicate browser upgrades; both must reject and only one worker owner can be registered.
